penalties_applied.name: b2c_at_scale_needed
penalties_applied.reason: This is a consumer utility app targeting individual Windows users; meaningful revenue requires thousands of paying users given typical $10–30 one-time price points for desktop utilities.

rationale: The buyer is an individual Windows consumer or small home-office user — a segment with very low willingness to pay for desktop utilities (most expect free tools, and free alternatives like dupeGuru already exist). There is no specific business role with a budget line, making `buyer_clarity` weak (4). The core product would need to be a downloadable Windows application with safe file-deletion logic, which requires native OS integration beyond what Claude prompts and a simple web page can deliver — `buildability_with_ai` scores just 3. Even if built, reaching enough paying consumers to generate meaningful revenue demands scale that is expensive and competitive to acquire.
solution_plan: This would be a Windows desktop app that scans folders for duplicate files by hash, shows a safe preview, and lets users delete duplicates with one click. Building it properly requires a compiled native or Electron app with filesystem access — not something the factory can ship as Claude prompts and a landing page; a real developer would be needed. Selling it means driving consumer traffic via SEO, app stores, or Reddit — high-volume, low-conversion channels that require sustained marketing spend. Even if live, support load from users accidentally deleting files they needed would create ongoing human-judgement issues. The free alternatives (dupeGuru, Duplicate Cleaner free tier) make paid conversion very hard. Drop.
notes: Failing build_gates: buildability_with_ai (3 < 6), buyer_clarity (4 < 6), willingness_to_pay (3 < 5). Saturated consumer utility category with strong free alternatives; not a fit for this factory's autonomous digital-service model.
